narrative.overview: I-ITSM is laid out like a hand-operated cricket ground scoreboard. The shell is painted board green; every live count, countdown and incident number hangs on it as a white tin plate with two pin holes, set in heavy condensed numerals that read from the back of a lecture hall. The working surfaces sit on a pale grass-grey ground in plain white panels, so the board carries the drama and the work stays calm.
keyCharacteristics: Board green shell and boards; white hung plates for every live number
One type family: Barlow for reading, Barlow Condensed for numbers, headings and plates
One reversed plate per screen for what needs attention now
SLA time drawn as twelve ball slots that fill as the window is used
Stepped, two-frame state changes; no easing anywhere

rules.name: The Reserved Paint Rule
rules.body: Priority colours appear only on P-tags and SLA danger states.

rules.name: The One Reversed Plate Rule
rules.body: Each screen hangs exactly one dark plate, and it always names the most urgent single item for that role.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: No third face. Numbers, incident IDs, countdowns and scores use Barlow Condensed with tabular figures; there is no monospace.

dos: Do hang every live number as a plate on a board, with a chalk caption under it.
Do give each screen one reversed plate for the most urgent single item, and only one.
Do set numbers, incident IDs and countdowns in Barlow Condensed with tabular figures.
Do change state in stepped frames; flip plates on new values.
donts: Don't use P1–P4 colours for anything but priority tags and SLA danger.
Don't add eased transitions, fades or animated chart entrances.
Don't reintroduce rounded pills, a monospace face, or the old navy rail.
Don't wrap content in same-size icon cards; hierarchy comes from scale, not boxes.
Don't tag healthy things: only outages and degraded services get a filled marker.
Don't put a caps caption above a plate's headline; lead words go in the detail line below it.
